Class JwtAuthorizationToken

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken
org.springframework.security.boot.jwt.authentication.JwtAuthorizationToken
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Principal, org.springframework.security.core.Authentication, org.springframework.security.core.CredentialsContainer
public class JwtAuthorizationToken extends org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken
Spring Security AbstractAuthenticationToken that represents an already-authorized JWT principal.

Unlike JwtAuthenticationToken, which is created from the raw credentials of an authentication attempt, this token is produced when the framework already trusts the principal — typically when a stateless service decodes a previously issued JWT and simply needs to thread the associated identity through the SecurityContext.

The token is structurally identical to JwtAuthenticationToken but its lifecycle is slightly different: the second constructor will erase any credentials it receives, mirroring the convention used by UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken's trusted-constructor pattern.

The optional sign, longitude and latitude fields allow the request to carry replay-protection and geo-location hints that downstream authorization filters can inspect.

Since:
3.0.0
Author:
[@Loong Wan](https://github.com/loong10k)

  • Constructor Details

    • JwtAuthorizationToken

      public JwtAuthorizationToken(Object principal, Object credentials)
      Builds an unauthenticated authorization token from a principal/credentials pair extracted from the inbound JWT. The token will report authenticated = false and is intended for use by an AuthenticationManager that still needs to perform a credential check.
      Parameters:
      principal - the principal to authorize, never null.
      credentials - the JWT string or other secret proving the principal's identity, never null.

    • JwtAuthorizationToken

      public JwtAuthorizationToken(Object principal, Object credentials, Collection<? extends org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority> authorities)
      Builds a trusted authorization token for an already-verified principal. Any credentials supplied are immediately erased so that the bearer material is not retained on the authorization-tier object.
      Parameters:
      principal - the trusted principal, never null.
      credentials - optional credentials; typically null or a transient token string that should not survive past construction.
      authorities - the granted authorities for the principal, may be null or empty.
